label: Weekend of Nov 13–15
status: Weekend complete — Toronto Jr Canadiens win the Challenger Cup (3-1 over Team Illinois)
note: Ranks are MHR’s Nov 11 ratings and move live as results come in. Game times are local to the rink. Many rinks stream on LiveBarn.

summary: CHAMPIONS: Toronto Jr Canadiens (CAN, 98.22) won the Little Caesars Challenger Cup, beating Team Illinois (#4, 97.11) 3-1 in the final at BELFOR. Toronto went 6-0 and outscored its opponents 28-3 over the weekend.

The final: Tristan Reynolds scored the opener in the 1st and the game-winner in the 2nd, finishing with 12 goals in six games. Colton Lantz made it 3-0, and Colton Dimmell had two assists. Caleb Bauer got Illinois on the board late in the 2nd, but Christian Arianna shut the door from there. Illinois couldn't score on its 3rd-period power plays, and the game ended with a pair of matching penalties at the buzzer.

Road to the final: Illinois beat Little Caesars 4-2 in the semifinals (Noah Mahery Moreau's winner with 5:21 left, after LC led 2-1 after one period). Toronto beat Nashville 5-1, scoring three goals in about 3½ minutes of the 1st.

Division winners: Toronto won Division A (4-0, three shutouts), Little Caesars won Division B (3-0-1), Team Illinois won Division C (4-0, two shutouts), and Nashville won Division D (3-0-1). Nashville got in only because Masters (#25) held Pittsburgh to a 2-2 tie Saturday night; the Penguins needed to win by four goals to take the division.

Other stories: Seacoast (#22, 94.37) came back from 2-0 down in the 3rd to tie Little Caesars 2-2, the only blemish on LC's record. Top Gun (#11, 96.25) started 0-2 but won its last two, including 5-2 over Windy City.

Note: Fox Motors (#27) played four games on the Challenger Cup schedule, against Boston Jr Eagles, Seacoast, Upper Canada College and Huron-Perth, and won all four. They're listed as a 14U/U15 entry, not in any of the four divisions, so they aren't in the standings, the bracket or the report card. Their games still count in the ratings.

Also: Chicago Mission (#6) swept its home-and-home with the Reapers. After Saturday's 4-3 shootout win, Mission won 3-0 at Mount Prospect on Sunday. Cash Cieslak scored the winner, and Michael Mufarreh had a power-play goal and an assist.

summary: Chicago Mission (#9, 91.58) gave the top-ranked Chicago Reapers (#1, 94.97) two one-goal games. The Reapers won 3-2 Saturday and 3-2 in overtime Sunday at Elk Grove. On Sunday, Mission scored a power-play goal with 3:11 left to force overtime, and the Reapers won it at 4:40 of OT after outshooting Mission 39-18. Losing twice by one goal to the #1 team actually raised Mission's rating, by about 0.16.

Elsewhere: Mid-Fairfield (#4, 93.86) beat Middlesex twice, 7-3 and 10-4, and Northern CT Nor'easters (#11, 91.42) beat NJ Rockets 5-3 and 10-2 before tying Middlesex 3-3 Sunday. Cleveland Barons (#8) swept Philadelphia Jr Flyers 3-1, 6-1 and 4-3. In Dallas, St. Louis beat the Dallas Stars 4-2, and Tampa Bay beat HB Detroit 5-3.
MN Lakers (#2), Anaheim (#3), Little Caesars (#4), Mid-Fairfield (#5), Woodbridge (#6) and Syracuse (#7) have no games listed this weekend.

summary: Shattuck St Mary's (#4, 94.44) won the Detroit round robin at 3-1. They clinched it Sunday by beating Bishop Kearney 4-3: Bishop Kearney (#3, 94.98) came back from 3-1 down to tie it 3-3 midway through the 3rd, and Shattuck scored the winner 26 seconds later.

Final standings: Shattuck 3-1 (beat Bishop Kearney 6-2 and 4-3, split with LC 1-5 and 3-0). Little Caesars (#8, 93.36) 2-2, including a 5-2 comeback win over Bishop Kearney. Bishop Kearney 1-3, with the #2-rated team in the country losing three of four, and its rating dropped from 95.55 to 94.98.
Mount St Charles (#2, 95.02) beat PAL Jr Islanders 9-1.
Chicago Reapers (#5, 93.64) beat Chicago Mission (#7, 93.37) 4-1 Saturday at Elk Grove. The rematch is today at 1:30 PM at Mount Prospect.
